key_concepts: Plants reproduce by sexual or asexual reproduction
Sexual reproduction fuses gametes and produces genetically different offspring
Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring without gamete fusion
Flower reproductive parts include receptacle, petal, sepal, pistil, and stamen
The stamen is the male part and includes the anther and filament
The pistil is the female part and includes the stigma, style, and ovary
Petals attract insects and sepals protect the flower bud
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
Fertilization occurs when a sperm cell fuses with an egg inside an ovule
After fertilization, each ovule develops into a seed and the ovary becomes fruit
Germination is the growth of a seed into a new plant and needs soil, water, and sunlight
Vegetative reproduction uses rhizomes, stolons, bulbs, tubers, or corms
